Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — Compact -> HighThru migration

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we look at our renewal: our engineering team is debating whether to bump to the HighThru tier or keep Compact and buy add-on throughput bundles. Our current usage is spiky (batch overnight, bursts during events) and we care a lot about per-token cost for embeddings.

Can you outline the recommended migration paths you typically see for customers with similar usage? Specifically:
- How to evaluate seat-based vs throughput bundles for a mixed workload
- Tradeoffs when downgrading later (credits/proration)
- Typical discount brackets for a multiyear commit vs month-to-month

Attaching a brief CSV of our last quarter usage. Would appreciate a short recommendation so we can decide before our renewal review next week.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Li
Head of AI Ops, Medialogic

Thanks for the context and attachment, Anna — this is helpful. High level first: both approaches are viable, we typically recommend the HighThru tier when predictable low-latency serving is the primary goal and prefix/KV cache benefits matter (saves tokens for chat-like workloads). Throughput bundles (metering credits) can be more cost-efficient for very spiky batch patterns.

A couple quick asks so I can give a concrete recommendation:
- Can you confirm % of requests that are embeddings vs generation? (CSV has timestamps but not label)
- Any hard latency SLOs for interactive traffic?

Ben (looping you in) — can you surface the common commercial structures we can offer (12/24 month commit bands, incremental seat credits, and downgrade protections)? I’ll draft two recommended paths for Anna once we have the split.

Next steps: Anna — if you can drop that split later today I’ll send a short pro/con grid + ballpark economics.

Best,

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Anna Li <anna.li@medialogic.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — Compact -> HighThru migration

Thanks for the data, Samir — that clarifies a lot. I’ve sketched two commercial options we commonly propose: 

Option A — HighThru Tier (recommended if interactive latency matters)
- 12-month term, 8x baseline seat allowance with 20% burst credits monthly
- 10% commit discount on list; additional 5% if you commit to a 24-month term
- Downgrade path: 30-day notice window; unused committed tokens converted to credits for 60 days
- Add-on: embedding cache optimization (one-time tuning) included as a professional services credit

Option B — Compact + Throughput Bundles (recommended if batch dominates)
- 12-month term; purchase throughput bundles that scale by 10TB token blocks
- Effective discount: typically 8% on bulk bundle purchases; pricing becomes competitive vs HighThru at >150% monthly variance
- Downgrade path: prorated refund of unused bundle capacity or conversion to add-on credits

Commercial flex we can offer for Medialogic: 5% additional onboarding credit if you sign within 14 days; we can lock a soft SLA for the first 90 days of migration.

Action items:
- Kimberly: can you prepare a simple cost example for both options using the CSV numbers?
- Anna/Samir: confirm whether interactive SLO is 200ms P95 for UI-facing calls.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 14:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — Compact -> HighThru migration

Anna — circling back with the example numbers attached and a recommended path. Summary:

- If your UI SLO is ~200ms P95 and ~30% of traffic is real-time generation, we recommend moving to HighThru with a 12-month commit. The combined savings from KV caching plus commit discount outweighs the bundle approach for your profile.
- Proposed commercial: 12-month HighThru, 10% commit discount, one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of first-quarter spend, and a 60-day downgrade credit window after go-live.
- If you want maximum unit-cost efficiency and are comfortable with more manual scaling, keep Compact + buy 2 throughput bundles as a stopgap and reevaluate after 3 months.

Next steps: I’ll upload a short quote to HubSpot and generate the DocuSign for a 12-month HighThru term with the onboarding credit. If you want the 2-month validation window written in, we can add a short clause to the SOW.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through the numbers tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
